answers.reason: As a junior professor without a central leadership office or senior rank, they are not automatically entitled to a seat in the central university senate.
University-wide budget allocation is reserved for central leadership, administration, and faculty heads rather than junior faculty.
In a strongly rank-based university, professorship appointments are reserved for higher-ranking office holders and full professors.
As the holder of a professorship in the faculty, the junior professor belongs to the professorial rank entitled to participate in faculty-level governance.
Holding a professorial office that involves teaching permits participation in faculty-level teaching committees.
As a professor who teaches in the faculty, the junior professor has the rank required to serve on the faculty examination board.
As a professor building up a research group, the junior professor has the rank to participate in faculty-level research funding rounds.
Because they hold a teaching professorship, they are permitted to take part in working groups below the faculty council level.
Holding a professorial rank allows the junior professor to participate in lower-level faculty decisions regarding teaching and research equipment.
Since higher rank permits participation in lower-level bodies, a junior professor may take part in operational faculty planning rounds.
